headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write/egress broadly while mem0 has no documented isolation, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP, so it can ingest mem0-produced content if the pair shares a workspace or file bridge. mem0 is a knowledge-management agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls. This is not provably blocked, but the shared-channel pathway is not guaranteed by the profiles, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF mem0 output is written into a VS Code workspace file that Roo Code reads
IF Roo Code treats file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep mem0 outputs in a separate folder not opened by Roo Code
Disable MCP servers for the Roo Code session
Add a manual review step before Roo Code acts on mem0 text
Prefix mem0 outputs with explicit non-instruction markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code has broad network egress and can read workspace files, while mem0 is a memory system that may store or surface sensitive context. If both touch the same workspace, Roo Code can transmit file contents to configured model APIs or MCP servers. The profiles do not prove PHI or secrets, so medium fits the default shared-workspace leakage path.
conditions: IF mem0 stores sensitive notes in files inside the shared workspace
IF Roo Code sends those files to a configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Store sensitive mem0 data outside the Roo Code workspace
Review Roo Code API endpoint settings before use
Disable browser and MCP tools for sensitive sessions
Use separate OS accounts or workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses with per-step approval; mem0 has no documented concurrency or locking surface. If mem0 and Roo Code share a workspace, concurrent edits can race on the same files or git state. The blast radius can include lost work or corrupted commits, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF mem0 and Roo Code operate on the same workspace directory
IF both modify the same file or git branch without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Review diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transaction coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and execute shell or git actions, so if it consumes mem0 output as authoritative, errors can cascade into real changes. mem0 is a knowledge-management agent and may emit unverified memory or summaries. Because Roo Code has downstream action authority, the pair creates a high-risk action chain.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses mem0 output as a source of truth
IF Roo Code then executes shell, git, or file actions based on that output
mitigations: Require human review of mem0-derived facts before action
Mark mem0 output as untrusted in prompts
Limit Roo Code to read-only mode for mem0-fed tasks
Compare mem0 claims against primary sources
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: Roo Code handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, while mem0 is a memory system that may retain user data. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because the data classes are not explicitly regulated here, medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF mem0 stores regulated or customer data that Roo Code also processes
IF Roo Code forwards that data to a provider or logs it under a different retention policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces
Check provider retention settings before use
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive projects
Review logging settings in Roo Code
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
